text:
samir: Heads-up: planning a minor but breaking change to the streaming frame shape for /v2/generate. moving from newline-delimited JSON lines with bare tokens to a framed envelope `\{"type\": \"chunk\", \"payload\": ...\}` so we can add cursor/meta without changing the token stream. this will break older SDKs that just read lines.

lena: Ack. Do we have a migration window? I'm guessing some customers run long-lived connections from browsers.

samir: We want a 30d deprecation window, but we should also ship a runtime-side compatibility shim for a graceful fallback. Proposal: if client sends `x-rw-client-features: bits=...` that advertises support for `framed-stream-v2`, we serve the new format. Otherwise the proxy translates v2 frames -> old ndjson tokens.

ben: Quick Q: is translating stateful (cursor) metadata safe? older clients will ignore it, but we also need to preserve token ordering and chunk boundaries. shim should emit token-only lines if client doesn't understand frames.

maria: Right. Implementation idea: shim sits at edge (nginx/lua or envoy filter) and strips the envelope, printing `payload.tokens` as ndjson. It must also convert event types: `{type: \"done\"}` -> final newline.

aj: Can we avoid adding a hot-path in the edge that does CPU work per token? Doing JSON decode/encode per chunk at 100k rps might cost us. Maybe implement a lightweight parser in C++ in the runtime side or add a flag to the streaming runtime to emit legacy format when `legacy=true` in request headers.

samir: Good point. Tradeoff: edge shim (fast deploy, flexible) vs runtime native support (more efficient but requires rollout). My preference: short-term edge shim for canary, long-term runtime flag.

ben: Agree. We should also include telemetry to measure how many clients advertise framing support. add two metrics: `client_features_count{framed_v2=1}` and `shim_translated_streams_total`.

maria: Also add a sticky cookie/response header so once a client negotiates framing we can prefer the native runtime path on subsequent connections: `x-rw-frame-preferred: 1` in responses.

lena: For SDKs: can we publish a tiny patch that authors call `transport.supportsFraming = true`? We'll include in the next minor release and add a runtime deprecation notice.

samir: Plan summary: 1) implement a lean edge shim (lua filter) that rewrites frames->ndjson for legacy clients, instrument `shim_translated_streams_total`; 2) add `x-rw-client-features` header to allow explicit capability advertising; 3) runtime change behind a feature flag `serve_framed_stream` to emit new format natively; 4) 30d deprecation notice + SDK patches and docs.

aj: Can I prototype the lua shim? I'll do a perf microbenchmark to ensure <5% p99 added latency at our baseline throughput.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: edge-lua-shim v0.1 -> gateway-canary-2 (samir, aj).

ben: We should add tests: a) old client (line reader) against new server w/ shim, b) new client (framed parser) against new server w/o shim, c) mixed concurrency test where some streams upgrade mid-connection.

maria: One more thing: we need to handle errors consistently. If shim sees malformed frames, return `420` with body `unsupported-stream-format` (so SDKs can surface clear error).

samir: Agree. I'll write an RFC follow-up with the exact header names, telemetry labels, and the fallback contract. Will ping SDK leads to coordinate release.

lena: sgtm. also add a short customer-facing blurb in docs explaining that streaming framing improves meta reliability and is opt-in for now.

runtime-bot: FYI: created ticket RW-3456 "streaming frame compatibility shim" and linked to this thread.

samir: Thanks all. Aj, let's sync tomorrow at 10 to pair on the lua filter and perf harness. :thumbsup:

aj: 👍 will bring a perf script and a minimal example client.

maria: I'll draft the SDK blurb and add a migration checklist.

samir: Closing notes: prioritize low-latency path if we can; shim only until runtime rollout. keep telemetry granular so we can measure client upgrade rate.
